renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: transcript_structures
  title: Transcript structures
  description: |-
    Each lane is one transcript of a gene drawn on a base-pair axis, with its exons as blocks and its coding sequence as taller blocks, coloured by novelty class. It answers how the isoforms of a gene differ in exon structure and which of them are known or new.
    How to read: lanes that share most blocks but differ in one are alternative splicing events. A novel class on a lane marks a transcript the reference annotation does not hold, so check its expression before trusting it.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-Sequence-Ontology/Specifications/master/gff3.md
  kind: transcript_structure
  roles:
    transcript_id: transcript_id
    gene_id: gene_id
    chrom: chrom
    start: start
    end: end
    feature: feature
    strand: strand
    sample: sample
    gene_name: gene_name
    transcript_class: transcript_class
    expression: expression

- component: card
  title: Transcripts in the annotation
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct transcripts, with the number of exon and CDS blocks beside it, and the bars rank the genes that carry the most isoforms. It answers how rich the annotation is and where the splicing complexity sits.
    How to read: genes with many isoforms are candidates for alternative splicing. A count close to the number of genes means one isoform per gene.
  column: transcript_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_name
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by isoform count
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Transcript expression
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median expression recorded by the annotation writer for its transcripts, with the lowest and highest value beside it, and the histogram shows the spread. It answers how strongly the annotated transcripts are expressed.
    How to read: expression is long-tailed, so a median far below the maximum is normal. A pile at zero marks transcripts present in the annotation but not observed.
    Note: each transcript counts once for every block it has, so transcripts with many exons weigh more. The expression unit is the one the writer used.
  column: expression
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: median, with the distribution

- component: table
  title: Exon and CDS blocks
  description: |-
    Each row is an exon or CDS block with its transcript, gene, chromosome, coordinates, strand, novelty class and expression. It answers the exact coordinates behind the structure drawing.
    How to read: filter by transcript class to list the novel transcripts, or by gene to see every isoform of it.
